title: Simple Food Chains
seo_title: Year 2 Science: Simple Food Chains Worksheets (What Eats What)
standard_code: Year 2: Living things and their habitats
standard_text: Describe how animals obtain their food from plants and other animals, using the idea of a simple food chain, and identify and name different sources of food.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 science worksheets on simple food chains: what eats what, reading arrows, putting chains in order and where our food comes from. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A food chain shows what eats what.
key_sub: It starts with a plant. The arrow means 'is eaten by'.
body_html:
How to think about it

A food chain shows what eats what.

  • It starts with a green plant.
  • The arrow means 'is eaten by'.
  • All our food comes from plants or animals.
Example

Grass → rabbit → fox. What does the fox eat?

Follow the arrow

Answer: the rabbit

Example

Where does an egg come from?

An animal

Answer: a hen

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the arrow points to the thing that gets eaten.
  • Thinking food chains start with an animal.
  • Thinking milk comes from a factory.

faq.a: A food chain shows what eats what, for example grass → rabbit → fox. The grass is eaten by the rabbit, and the rabbit is eaten by the fox.

faq.q: Why do food chains start with a plant?
faq.a: Plants make their own food using sunlight. Animals cannot, so they eat plants or other animals.

faq.q: Where does our food come from?
faq.a: All our food comes from plants (bread, apples, chips) or animals (milk, eggs, fish).
